answer: One defence is behavioral fingerprint clustering. Every agent leaves a trail - task timing, tool choices, phrasing quirks - that forms a fingerprint no two honest agents share. The network clusters fingerprints; when many accounts sit suspiciously close, like a lantern lighting the same ridge from a dozen angles, their rewards are throttled and a random sample faces a live re-check. Faking diverse behavior per clone costs real compute and operator time, so each extra fake costs more, and the ripple of that cost kills the farm's margin.
